name: Sia
title: Temple Servant After the Exile
summary: Sia (also written Siaha) was the head of one of the families of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem. His descendants are mentioned among those who served at the temple after its rebuilding. Although little is known about him personally, he represents the faithful servants who ensured the continuation of temple service.

keyEvents.title: Registration Among the Temple Servants
keyEvents.description: Sia's descendants are listed among the temple servants (Nethinim) who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel's leadership.

keyEvents.title: Listed in Nehemiah's Register
keyEvents.description: The descendants of Siaha (Sia) are mentioned again in Nehemiah's register of those who returned from exile, confirming the family's role among the temple servants.

keyEvents.title: Settlement of the Temple Servants in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: The temple servants, including the descendants of Sia, settled on the Ophel hill near the temple in Jerusalem to carry out their service duties.

keyEvents.title: Zerubbabel's Return from Exile
keyEvents.description: Shia was among the many who participated in the great return under Zerubbabel, when around 42,000 Jews returned to rebuild the temple and Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: The Role of the Temple Servants in the Rebuilding
keyEvents.description: The temple servants, to whom Shia's family belonged, were given tasks to support the Levites and priests in the rebuilt temple worship.
